keep.body:
Look around. Everyone’s caught up in their own story. Nobody’s judging you. Nobody’s watching. And if they are, who cares?

Even if you’re stuck - mobility issues, chronic illness, or just your personality - you’ve still got options. I pick up my camera. I talk. I share. I put myself out there.

Filming isn’t just about content—it’s about beating isolation. Turning loneliness into conversation. Creating connections, right from this pizza place.

Talking to a camera feels weird at first, but behind that lens is someone listening. No one’s watching - until they are. And when they finally tune in, they’re usually glad I showed up.

keep.body: Talking to the camera helps me climb out when depression pulls me under. It gives me structure, reflection, and a sense of connection, like I’m reminding myself I’m still here, still trying. It’s one of the ways I lift myself up.

drops.body:
As spiritual entrepreneurs, we often hold space for others - but who holds space for us when the weight hits?
Talking to the camera has become one of my ways to reconnect, process, and rise.
It’s not just content. It’s practice. Presence. A form of self-witnessing.
This is how I move energy. This is one way I come back to myself.

keep.body:
Today.
Not tomorrow.
Not when you’re “ready.”
Not after one more conversation, one more excuse, one more perfect condition.

You’ve dreamed it. You’ve talked it to death.
You’ve imagined a thousand versions of it.
But you haven’t done it.

And you know that.

So don’t think. Don’t plan. Don’t overexplain.
Don’t check with friends. Don’t wait for a sign.

This is the sign.

keep.body: Fez isn’t easy—but it’s not impossible either. If you can take small steps here and there, with some space between, and have someone by your side—it’s doable. The alleys are tight, the crowds intense, and yeah—every couple of hours you’ll hit a step or two. But people are kind, always jumping in to help (sometimes a little too eager). It’s chaotic, ancient, alive. And somehow, the adrenaline takes the edge off the pain. If you move slowly, with patience and grit, Fez will meet you halfway.
